title: Local lifting of the G-ring property through an adic quotient
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal and assume that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. If $A/I$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then $A$ is a G-ring. No hypothesis on characteristic, dimension, or universal catenarity is imposed.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 2, equation (5.1), printed p.9; Appendix A, Definition A.1(2), printed p.14, and the G-ring LLP assertion printed p.15, citing Rotthaus [14] (1979). Local case of that semilocal lifting theorem.

proof.text: Apply the finite-domain generic-fibre criterion to the local ring $A$. Fix an arbitrary finite $A$-algebra domain $B$; its structure map need not be injective. The criterion gives that $B$ is Noetherian semilocal. Put $J=IB$ and $\mathfrak r=\operatorname{Jac}(B)$. Finite-module completeness gives $B\simeq\varprojlim_nB/J^n$, since $J^n=I^nB$.

source.place: Theorem 3, p.176, reduction to finite domain algebras by Lemma 1.

proof.text:
Every maximal ideal of $B$ contracts to $\mathfrak m$: finite algebras are integral and maximal ideals contract to maximal ideals. Conversely every prime containing $\mathfrak mB$ is maximal, since $B/\mathfrak mB$ is integral over the field $A/\mathfrak m$ and has dimension zero. Thus $J\subseteq\mathfrak r=\sqrt{\mathfrak mB}$. The radical-power bound gives $\mathfrak r^t\subseteq\mathfrak mB\subseteq\mathfrak r$ for some $t$, so the two filtrations are cofinal. Consequently
$$C:=\varprojlim_nB/\mathfrak r^n=\widehat A\otimes_A B\simeq\prod_{\mathfrak n\in\operatorname{Max}B}\widehat{B_{\mathfrak n}}.$$
Here the finite-extension completion theorem at $\mathfrak m$ gives the displayed product and tensor identifications. Each factor is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal extended from $\mathfrak n$. Hence $C$ is Noetherian, and $\mathfrak rC=\operatorname{Jac}(C)$, so $JC\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(C)$.

source.place: Lemma 1 and conventions p.173; standard finite semilocal completion identifications (Stacks 07N9).

proof.text: The algebra $B/J$ is finite over $A/I$, hence of finite type (module generators also generate it as an algebra). Finite-type stability of G-rings makes $B/J$ a G-ring. It is semilocal, so the semilocal G-ring criterion makes it quasi-excellent and therefore Nagata. Apply Nagata lifting to the already verified $J$-complete ring $B$: it is Nagata. Each domain $B_{\mathfrak n}$ is then local Nagata and has reduced maximal completion. The product description above shows that $C$ is reduced.

source.place: Theorem 1 (Marot), pp.173–174, used in Theorem 3 Claim 1, p.177; existing Nagata-lifting route supplies the needed reducedness.

proof.text: For every nonmaximal $\mathfrak Q\supseteq JC$ put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak Q\cap B$, $U_{\mathfrak p}=\widehat{B_{\mathfrak p}}$ and $T_{\mathfrak Q}=\widehat{C_{\mathfrak Q}}$. The completed-local comparison theorem applies to $B/J$, giving canonical regular, faithfully flat maps $U_{\mathfrak p}\to T_{\mathfrak Q}$. This asserts regularity only after completing the source $B_{\mathfrak p}$; no G-ring property of $B$ is used.

For every prime $\mathfrak p\supseteq J$ of $B$, the domain $B/\mathfrak p$ is a G-ring, being a quotient of $B/J$. As a semilocal G-ring it is Nagata. Its localizations at maximal ideals are Nagata domains, so their maximal completions are reduced. Apply the finite-extension completion product theorem to the finite $A$-algebra $B/\mathfrak p$. Exactness of completion on finite $A$-modules, and the natural tensor description of completion, identify its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion with $C/\mathfrak pC$. Thus $C/\mathfrak pC$ is reduced, i.e. $\mathfrak pC$ is radical. This checks the reduced-prime-extension hypothesis needed for primary descent, also for maximal $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Theorem 3, Claim 4 and (4.3), pp.178–179: reduced prime extensions needed for the primary decomposition argument.

proof.text: It suffices to show that every singular prime $\mathfrak P$ of $C$ contracts to a nonzero ideal of $B$. The singular-ideal patching theorem applies: $B$ is a semilocal Nagata domain, and all the required completed comparisons are regular. It gives a nonzero radical ideal $D\subseteq C$, with $DT_{\mathfrak Q}=s(U_{\mathfrak Q\cap B})T_{\mathfrak Q}$ above $J$, where $s(U)$ is the intersection of the singular primes of $U$. It also says every singular $\mathfrak P$ of $C$ is nonzero.

source.place: Theorem 3 construction of D and Claims 1–2, pp.176–177.

proof.text: Fix such a singular $\mathfrak P$. If a nonmaximal prime contains $\mathfrak P+JC$, the patching theorem gives $D\subseteq\mathfrak P$; take $E=D$. The compatible ideals for descent are $e_{\mathfrak p}=s(U_{\mathfrak p})$, one and the same ideal for all $\mathfrak Q$ over $\mathfrak p$. Otherwise take $E=\mathfrak P$. In this case every nonmaximal $\mathfrak Q\supseteq JC$ avoids some element of $\mathfrak P$, so $ET_{\mathfrak Q}=T_{\mathfrak Q}$, and take $e_{\mathfrak p}=U_{\mathfrak p}$. In both cases $0\ne E\subseteq\mathfrak P$.

source.place: Theorem 3, cases 1–2, p.176, and Claim 3, p.178.

proof.text:
Apply compatible-formal-ideal descent to this $E$. Step 4 provides faithful flatness of each completed comparison, step 5 gives radicality of every prime extension above $J$, and step 7 supplies a single compatible ideal for each $\mathfrak p$. Thus for $a_n=(E+J^nC)\cap B$ and every $n\ge1$,
$$a_nC=E+J^nC,\qquad a_{n+1}+J^n=a_n.$$
The boundary case in step 7 is included: its compatibility condition uses unit ideals and makes no affineness or positive-dimensional-fibre assumption.

We now give the nonzero-contraction argument of Lemma 2 explicitly. Since $E\ne0$ and $\bigcap_r(\operatorname{Jac}C)^r=0$ by Krull intersection, choose $r\ge1$ with $E\not\subseteq(\operatorname{Jac}C)^r$. Because $E\subseteq a_rC$, some $f_r\in a_r$ has image outside $(\operatorname{Jac}C)^r$. Recursively choose $f_{n+1}\in a_{n+1}$ with $f_{n+1}-f_n\in J^n$, using $a_{n+1}+J^n=a_n$. Then $f_n\equiv f_r\pmod{J^r}$ for every $n\ge r$.

source.place: Lemma 2, pp.174–175, choose a nonzero-compatible residue and lift it successively.

proof.text: The sequence is $J$-adic Cauchy: for $k\ge n\ge r$, $f_k-f_n\in J^n$. Since $B$ is $J$-complete, its compatible residue classes give $f\in B$ with $f-f_n\in J^n$ for every $n\ge r$. In particular the image of $f$ in $C$ is congruent to that of $f_r$ modulo $J^rC\subseteq(\operatorname{Jac}C)^r$. The latter image was nonzero in this quotient, so $f\ne0$.

source.place: Lemma 2, pp.174–175, convergence and the nonzero residue.

proof.text: Fix $n\ge r$. For all $k\ge n$ the nesting of the $a_k$ gives $f_k\in a_n$, so the class of $f$ in the finite $B$-module $B/a_n$ belongs to every $J^k(B/a_n)$. Krull intersection, with $J\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(B)$, makes this class zero. Hence $f\in a_n$ for every $n\ge r$, and its image in $C/E$ belongs to every $J^n(C/E)$. Krull intersection again, now over $C$ with $JC\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(C)$, gives $f\in E\cap B\subseteq\mathfrak P\cap B$. This proves $\mathfrak P\cap B\ne0$.

source.place: Lemma 2, conclusion p.175; Theorem 3 conclusion p.179.

proof.text: Therefore no singular prime of $C$ contracts to $(0)$ in $B$. Every $C_{\mathfrak P}$ with $\mathfrak P\cap B=(0)$ is regular local. Since the finite $A$-algebra domain $B$ was arbitrary, the finite-domain generic-fibre criterion proves that $A$ is a G-ring. Neither a characteristic restriction nor universal catenarity entered any step.

source.place: Theorem 3, final application of Lemma 1, p.179.

proof_origin.place: Rotthaus (1979), Lemma 1, Lemmas 2–4, Corollaries 4.1–4.2 and Theorem 3, pp.173–179; read online. Not archived in literature/, archival copy WANTED. Adapted using existing Nagata-lifting nodes.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q144-7b9c7dd7f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no changes; the full review is in review.md. Rotthaus 1979 and Kurano–Shimomoto are not in literature/, so I checked each new statement by my own proof, not against the source. The item statement is unchanged, it is not in a cycle, and its only citer (lem-per-qe-minimal-formal-defect step 3) uses exactly what it states. All 12 steps check against the cited statements. Step 1: B is finite over the complete ring A, so B is J-complete (finite-module-complete node). Step 2: Max B lies over m, r^t ⊆ mB ⊆ r, and 07N9 gives C = Â⊗B = ∏ (B_n)^ with rC = Jac C. Step 3: B/J is finite type over A/I, hence a G-ring (07PV), quasi-excellent (semilocal-g-ring-j2) and Nagata (07QV); adic-nagata-lifting makes B Nagata, and C is reduced by 032U and 0331. Step 5: B/p is a G-ring and Nagata, and 07N9, 00MA and 00MB identify C/pC with a reduced product, so pC is radical. Step 7 picks E = D or E = P with a single e_p for each p; it is correctly elementary. Steps 9–11 carry the Krull-intersection argument of Rotthaus's Lemma 2; the hypotheses J ⊆ Jac B and JC ⊆ Jac C are both checked. All four new nodes are true. (1) finite-domain-generic-test: forward because finite-type algebras over a G-ring are G-rings; backward through finite subalgebras B ⊆ κ' over R/q, using the allowed noninjective map R → B. (2) completed-local-comparison: the map of completions is flat local and its closed fibre is the completed generic formal fibre of the G-ring B/p, which is geometrically regular; with a complete source this gives a regular map. (3) formal-singular-ideal-patching: C is excellent and reduced, so s(C) ≠ 0, s(C) ⊆ D and s(C)T_Q = s(T_Q) = s(U_p)T_Q; D ⊆ P follows from ascent and descent of regularity. (4) compatible-formal-ideal-adic-descent: proved by taking a minimal point of Supp(F/aĈ), applying Matsumura 23.2 with pC radical, preservation of length and a local-cohomology argument; the single e_p is essential. I also tested the small cases J = 0, V(J) = Max, a transcendental curve (correctly excluded), and unit or zero E. No new node restates the item or one of its clauses (D1/D2). A DAG-wide search for duplicates found none; the nearest candidates (check-pairs-of-primes, 07PT, local-closed-fibre-criterion, qe-rotthaus-finite-boundary) are different statements. Form B1–B9 holds: statements only, unsplit, from/via/same_as filled, four kinds of search recorded, stmt_deps equal to the citations. I accept the tool_uses: they are generic commutative-algebra lemmas from sk-thm-p1 and 07QV (sk-prop-a1-kummer), all declared. WANTED: an archived copy of Rotthaus 1979 and of Kurano–Shimomoto.
